Our solution is live in 40+ countries, used by 550+ customers, and automates 70,000+ processes every day, including for Fortune 500 companies. As one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups, our success stems from deep expertise in technology and business processes, delivering a product with outstanding product-market fit, proven by a growing global customer base.

We've recently welcomed Goldman Sachs Alternatives as a growth investor, and we're now expanding into the UK and USA. We are just getting started. Ready to build the future? Join BLP Digital today.

About the role

We're hiring a Strategic Value Engineer (Presales) to shape and win enterprise ERP automation decisions: you reframe problems, quantify the cost of inaction, and prove value through tailored workshops and demos. Partnering with an AE, you own technical leadership, value articulation, and de-risking security/integration, building alignment across CFO/CIO-led buying committees.

 

What you'll own

Insight-led discovery and deal shaping

  • Practice insight selling: challenge the customer's initial framing, introduce a sharper point of view on where value is actually trapped (exceptions, approvals, master data, controls), and reframe urgency using cost-of-inaction.

  • Lead discovery across CFO/CIO/Shared Services/Procurement to uncover operational bottlenecks and decision friction, and translate that into a crisp target-state narrative and mutual action plan.

Solution design and technical leadership

  • Architect a tailored solution: scope, rollout approach, integration pattern, security posture, and success criteria.

  • Run deep dives with IT/security and articulate how blp works in enterprise environments (ERP digital twin, data synchronization, governance and controls).

Demos, workshops, and executive storytelling

  • Deliver high-impact demos that map to customer workflows (P2P, AP, S2P) and prove outcomes, not features.

  • Facilitate workshops that turn stakeholder skepticism into a tangible blueprint and path to value.

Value engineering (business case support)

  • Build a credible value narrative: labor productivity gains, cycle time reduction, compliance/control improvements, and stack simplification.

  • Support champions and the AE with executive-ready business-case inputs, impact ranges, and rollout economics, flagging risk to the deal early rather than late.

Competitive positioning

  • Position blp against point tools and fragmented stacks (OCR/IDP/workflow/process mining/RPA) with an "end-to-end + exceptions-first" narrative.

  • Help the deal team land a clear "why now" anchored in operational risk, ERP program success, and enterprise scale requirements.

 

What we're looking for

Must-haves

  • 3–8+ years in Value Engineering / Presales / Solution Consulting / ERP process consulting (or equivalent in finance/procurement operations with strong customer-facing chops).

  • Demonstrated ability to run insight-based discovery (Challenger-style): you can respectfully push back, quantify impact, and build conviction across a buying committee.

  • Comfort with senior stakeholders (CFO/CIO/Head of Shared Services): you can lead without authority.

  • Strong workshop facilitation and demo craft: story, structure, and objection handling.

  • Ability to connect technical realities to business outcomes (FTE capacity, cycle time, controls, compliance risk, TCO).

Strong plus

  • SAP exposure (S/4, ECC, Public/Private Cloud) or multi-ERP environments.

  • Finance/process knowledge: AP, invoice processing, S2P/P2P, exception handling, approvals, master data workflows.

  • Experience competing against legacy vendors and "patchwork stacks."

Language

  • Fluent in English and another major European language, preferably German, depending on territory.

 

What you'll get

  • A product that wins. blp's solution consistently outperforms competitors. Your job is to open more doors.

  • Uncapped earnings. High, realistic OTEs with uncapped commission.

  • Real ownership. Choose annually to take your variable compensation in cash or company shares.

  • Growth and autonomy. Build your own success path in a rapidly scaling, internationally expanding company.

  • Continuous learning. Structured onboarding and ongoing coaching to help you excel.

  • Exceptional team. Join a group of ambitious, collaborative colleagues who push each other to achieve excellence.

 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

title: Finance & AI Automation Intern (Remote Part-time)
description:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.

Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. The category is growing rapidly because AI doesn't work on bad data. Behind the product sits a group of three companies in two currencies, and a small finance team that keeps all of it correct. We're hiring a Finance & AI Automation Intern to run core finance processes and automate the manual work out of them.

About Us

Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing.

Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo.

The Role

You'll join the Finance team that covers Soda Data NV (Belgium), Soda Data Inc. (US) and NannyML NV, the Belgian company we acquired in 2025. The work is real from week one: invoice processing, month-end reporting, payroll data preparation, expense management, and intercompany recharges across three entities, two currencies and three accounting systems.

The second half of the job is making that work disappear. Finance at Soda builds agentically: Claude and other AI tools are part of the daily workflow, not an experiment on the side. You'll learn a process, run it until you know it cold, and then automate it. Sometimes that means an AI agent on GitHub, sometimes a well-designed formula - you pick the right tool and defend the choice. Accuracy is the bar for both: in finance, 99% right is wrong, so every automation ships with the checks and reconciliations that prove its output.

What You'll Do

  • Run core finance processes: invoice processing, month-end reporting, payroll data preparation, expense management, and intercompany recharges. Learn them, run them, own them.
  • Automate them: with Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub and the Soda MCP, or with smart spreadsheet design when that is the better tool.
  • Build in the checks: reconciliations and controls in everything you automate, so the output is verified before anyone else has to look at it.
  • Document as you go: process documentation that a colleague and an AI agent can both follow.
  • Support the wider Finance team: reporting, analysis, and ad-hoc projects across our Belgian and US entities.

Hiring Process

1.      Application with a few short questions

2.      Recorded video interview (3 questions, in your own time)

3.      20-minute interview

4.      Take-home assignment (plan for 5-6 hours)

5.      45-minute deep dive on your assignment

6.      Final interview

We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3-5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.

Requirements

•     A finance background: studying towards or recently completed a degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.

•     Proof that you build: you've used AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) and/or built automations, scripts, or advanced spreadsheet solutions, and you can show us one and explain how you checked its output.

•     Accuracy as a habit: you're the person who notices the 780 that should have been 800, and you don't sign off on numbers you haven't verified.

•     Independent with new tools: you can pick up GitHub, MCP-based integrations, and finance systems without a course.

•     Proactive: you spot the manual work and come with a plan for it. You'd rather build the workflow than do the task fifteen more times.

•     Fluent English, written and spoken.

•     European business hours: fully remote from any compatible time zone, or hybrid if you're near Amsterdam.

Good to Have

•     Experience with accounting software (e.g. Exact Online, QuickBooks) or ERP systems.

•     Exposure to Python, SQL, or API-based automation.

•     Prior startup or fast-paced work experience.

Benefits

What We Offer

•     €1,250 - €1,750 per month, depending on experience.

•     A clear path to a permanent role if you perform: 3-month contractor engagement first, extended as it works.

•     Fully remote and flexible working, or hybrid if you're near Amsterdam.

•     All the tokens you need, across all frontier models.

•     Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement. This is not a coffee-and-observe internship - you operate as part of the Finance team.

•     Start: As soon as possible, aiming for the beginning of October 2026

Our Values

We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful product and roadmap decisions.

❤️ Why you will love to join Soda

•     You own processes, not tickets: what you automate is yours to design, and behind it is a list of things nobody here has built yet.

•     Be part of a transformation: data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it.

•     Ownership from day one: if you see a bottleneck, you remove it.

•     International culture: colleagues in 12+ countries.

•     Work on your own terms: fully remote, flexible hours.

😡 What you might not love

•     Rapidly changing priorities: our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done.

•     Flexibility required: you will have to learn new things all the time.

 

Join us to elevate our finance team to the next level!

We're hiring one person to own content at Soda, end to end.

Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues.

The Role

The website. Technical blogs, webinars, and product videos. Your own content and following.

One person cannot hand-make all of that. So you'll build the system that can. That isn't a stretch goal or a second phase - we don't think the job exists without it.

You'll join the Growth team reporting to a co-founder.

What you might call yourself. Content engineer, technical content marketer, growth engineer, marketing engineer, GTM engineer, developer advocate, technical writer who got bored, or nothing in particular. We've seen this job posted under every one of those. We don't care what's on your CV. You need to be able to write and you need to be able to build, and almost nobody can do both.

Why this is a real problem and not a content calendar. The expertise is already in the building. Founders who have argued about this category for a decade. Customer engineers who spend their week inside broken pipelines at Fortune 500s. Customers who will tell you things nobody has published anywhere. Almost none of it gets written down, and what does get out is hand-made, one piece at a time, by people who have other jobs. Your job is to get it out of their heads and onto the internet, at a volume that is only possible with a machine behind it.

Taste is the bar. Anti-slop is the whole point. An engine that ships slop faster has negative value, and most of them do. We're hiring for the judgment to look at an accurate, competent, lifeless draft and bin it - then work out what the pipeline did wrong and fix it. The engine has to write in distinct voices: a founder sounds nothing like a customer engineer, and the output should sound like them, not like a model. Your own profile and following is part of how we'll know it works. If it can't make you sound good, it won't make anyone else sound good either.

What this is not. You'll write code every day, but this is not a software engineering job. We're not hiring you to build product, and if you're a backend, data, or platform engineer looking for your next engineering role, this isn't it. It's also not a traditional marketing or DevRel role: no agency to brief and no conference circuit.

Requirements

  • You can write, and you can tell good writing from bad: send us something you wrote that a technical audience actually read. The most important line in this ad.
  • Serious prompt engineering: multi-step LLM pipelines with structured outputs and evals, not chatting with a model. You know why the naive version produces slop.
  • 3+ years building things that go to market: technical content, growth engineering, marketing engineering, GTM engineering, DevRel, marketing ops, RevOps, or a founder background. Nobody agrees what to call this job yet. Titles vary; portfolios don't.
  • Enough code to be autonomous: Python or TypeScript, APIs, webhooks, a database. Nothing should be blocked waiting for an engineer. We build agentically here - Claude Code, MCP servers, and agent skills are the daily workflow.
  • Enough data fluency to be credible: you're writing for Staff Data Engineers and CDOs. You can hold your own on pipelines, data quality, and warehouses.
  • Generalist instinct: you find the constraint and fix it, and you'd rather build the workflow than do the task fifteen more times.
  • Independence: you don't need hand-holding in a distributed, async team across 12+ countries.
  • Fluent English.

Good to Have

  • You've grown a technical audience of your own: newsletter, blog, LinkedIn, open source, YouTube.
  • Content, growth, or DevRel in data, developer tools, or infrastructure.
  • Agentic workflows shipped to real users: MCP servers, Claude skills, tool-using agents.
  • You can shoot and cut video yourself.
  • Data quality, data management, or data observability industry experience.

Benefits

  • Compensation: $120,000-$130,000 / €110,000-€120,000 per year + equity - the same band wherever you live. We don't discount for geography.
  • Fully remote (US or EU-based), with offices in Brooklyn if you want one.
  • All the tokens you need, across all frontier models.
  • Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement.
  • Colleagues in 12+ countries.

Our Values

We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful decisions.

❤️ Why you will love to join Soda

  • Be part of a transformation: data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it.
  • Ownership from day one: if you see a bottleneck, you remove it.
  • International culture: colleagues in 12+ countries.
  • Work on your own terms: fully remote, flexible hours.
  • Paid the same wherever you are: one band for the US and Europe, no geographic discount.
  • Your name on the work: you build your own audience on company time, and we want you to.
  • Direct line to the founders: how Soda talks about the category gets decided with you in the room.

😡 What you might not love

  • Rapidly changing priorities: our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done.
  • Flexibility required: you will have to learn new things all the time.
  • You will kill a lot of your own output: accurate and lifeless still goes in the bin.
  • Judged on output, not architecture: an elegant pipeline nobody reads from is a failure.

Hiring Process

  1. 15-minute phone screen - with a founder
  2. Short Assignment
  3. Craft deep dive (90 min)
  4. Culture fit (1 hour)

We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3-5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.

description:
About Genesis AI

Genesis AI builds the simulation platform powering the next generation of robotics and embodied AI. Our flagship product, Genesis World, is a unified multi-physics simulation engine paired with Nyx, our in-house GPU-accelerated, path-traced photorealistic renderer. Together they provide a platform for training robotics and embodied AI at scale; letting teams simulate complex physical worlds with high fidelity and speed, from a laptop to datacenter-grade GPUs, and close the gap between simulation and the real world.

About the Role

A simulator is only as useful as the content that runs inside it. Training embodied agents at scale means large volumes of assets that are simultaneously physically valid and visually convincing and that is a pipeline problem before it is an art problem.

We're hiring a Senior Engineer to build the path from raw input to sim-ready asset: geometry from a range of sources going in; clean meshes, correct collision proxies, plausible physical properties, materials that hold up under a path tracer, and reliable metadata coming out.

The bar is throughput and repeatability. An asset that needs a human pass to be usable doesn't scale, so the pipeline has to make good decisions on its own and flag the cases where it can't.

Part of that autonomy comes from agents embedded in the graph itself. Nodes can call models to produce input content, drive generation, pick parameters, interpret a mesh before deciding how to treat it, or judge whether a result is acceptable. Making that reliable is its own engineering problem: agents are non-deterministic, they fail in ways a mesh operator doesn't, and they need guardrails, structured outputs, retries and verification around them. You'll be building that as a first-class part of the pipeline rather than bolting it on.

You'll work closely with the stakeholders, who set direction and priorities. You own the technical design and the implementation and you're expected to bring enough pipeline experience to challenge the plan where it needs challenging.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain the end-to-end asset pipeline, from ingestion through to validated output

  • Design agent-driven nodes that generate input content and make decisions inside the graph, with the structured outputs, guardrails and fallbacks that make them dependable in batch

  • Develop automated processing stages: mesh repair, retopology, decimation and LODs, UV unwrapping and texel density normalization, collision proxy generation

  • Derive physical properties so assets behave correctly in simulation: mass, inertia, contact parameters, articulation setup

  • Handle appearance: material conversion to PBR, texture processing, baking, and color management so assets render correctly in Nyx

  • Define and enforce asset standards (units, orientation, pivots, naming, provenance) and build the validators that reject noncompliant assets before they reach the library

  • Scale the pipeline to large batch runs, with caching, versioning and selective reprocessing when a stage changes

  • Build quality checks into the pipeline itself: physics stability harnesses, render smoke tests, automated evaluation of generated content, comparison on reprocessed assets

  • Work with the rendering, physics and research teams on what sim-ready needs to mean for each downstream use

What We're Looking For (ideally)

  • 5+ years building content or asset pipelines in games, VFX, simulation, or 3D tooling, with ownership of a pipeline in production

  • Deep knowledge of 3D asset formats and their quirks: USD, glTF, FBX, OBJ, plus physics description formats such as URDF or MJCF

  • Strong Python and C++ where processing needs to be fast

  • Hands-on mesh processing expertise: remeshing, decimation, UV generation, repair operations, convex decomposition, and a clear sense of how each one fails

  • Solid command of PBR material authoring, texture baking and color spaces

  • Experience driving DCC tools headlessly (Blender, Houdini, Maya) and building batch or distributed job systems around them

  • Practical experience putting LLM or agent calls into production systems: prompting, tool use, structured output, cost and latency control, and handling non-determinism

  • Understanding of what makes an asset physically valid in a simulator: visual versus collision geometry, mass properties, contact behavior, numerical stability

  • Judgment about quality bars, including when an asset is good enough and when it isn't

Nice to Have

  • Experience processing output from generative or reconstruction-based 3D sources, and evaluating that output automatically

  • Agent frameworks, orchestration and eval tooling applied to content generation

  • OpenUSD at scale: composition, layering, MaterialX

  • Semantic annotation and dataset curation at volume

  • Exposure to simulation stacks such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim or similar

  • Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry

  • $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.

  • Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.

The team

Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.

The role

A Front End Design Engineer thinks in finished interfaces, not mockups or components in isolation. A technical reviewer at a notified body spends their day inside a 400-page technical file, cross-referencing clauses, checking test reports against standards, and deciding whether a medical device is safe to sell. Today they do that in Word, Acrobat and a spreadsheet someone built in 2011. The interface they use decides how fast they work and whether they trust the AI sitting next to them.

You own that interface. Layout, typography, interaction, motion, the design system underneath it, and the React that ships it. You decide how a reviewer sees a finding, how they correct a model that got it wrong, and how a hundred fields of dense regulatory data become something a person can actually read. You sketch it, build it, ship it, then sit next to someone using it and find out what you got wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.

What we're looking for

We care far more about taste and engineering strength than about matching a list of tools. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in React, Svelte, Vue or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, craft and speed are not.

What we're actually screening for:

  • You've designed and built an interface that real people used every day. Not a Dribbble shot, not a component library nobody adopted. Something that shipped, got used, and got better.

  • You have taste, and you can defend it. Typography, spacing, motion, hierarchy. You notice when something is a few pixels off and you can explain why it matters.

  • You build the whole thing. Design, frontend, the state and data it sits on. You don't hand the code to someone else once the Figma is done, and you don't hand the design to someone else once the code is.

  • You can design for density. Expert users, complex workflows, hundreds of fields on a screen. Making that clear is much harder than making a landing page beautiful.

  • You go to the source. You'll watch a technical reviewer work through a real file, and you'll design for what they actually do rather than what the process diagram says.

Signals we like, none of them required:

design engineering or front-end roles at somewhere like Linear, Vercel, Notion or Figma, a design system you built and maintained, work on interfaces where people review or correct AI output, founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup.

This is probably not for you if

  • You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.

  • You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.

What you get

  • Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar

  • Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room

  • Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly

  • Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster

  • A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics

If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices and 68% (and growing!) of NHS Trusts.

Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book that lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.

That sounds cool — what does a Customer Success Manager have to do with it?

Accurx works with 41 of the 42 NHS ICBs in primary care and is growing fast in secondary care. The relationships that make that possible — the trust, the renewals, the accounts that stay with us even when competitors come knocking on price — are owned by our Customer Success team.

We’re hiring three CSMs to grow the team across both primary and secondary care. You’ll own a portfolio of enterprise NHS accounts end-to-end, from implementation through to renewal. In primary care, it’s about protecting and deepening relationships that are already strong. In secondary care, it’s about building them from scratch in a market where Accurx Scribe is winning big and growing fast. Either way, it’s about being the person NHS organisations trust — the one who knows their priorities, anticipates problems before they arise, and makes Accurx genuinely indispensable.

The challenges you’ll solve as a Customer Success Manager

  • Own your NHS accounts end-to-end. You’ll manage a portfolio of 5–11 ICB or Trust enterprise accounts — building relationships, driving adoption, leading renewals, and keeping Accurx sticky even when the NHS is in flux. You’re the person your customers call first.

  • Build trust where Accurx is new. In secondary care, we’re expanding quickly into a more complex environment. You’ll help NHS Trusts get real outcomes from Accurx Scribe — building processes that don’t yet exist and earning the kind of trust we’ve spent years building in primary care.

  • Be a connector, not just an account manager. You’ll work across marketing, implementation, transformation, commercial ops, and finance. The best CSMs here don’t just manage accounts — they bring the voice of the customer back into the business and make things better for the whole team.

  • Build the playbook as you go. The team is scaling and many of our processes are still being written. You’ll contribute to and shape how account management works at Accurx. What works gets codified; what doesn’t gets challenged.

  • Navigate the NHS with patience and precision. NHS organisations are under enormous pressure — restructuring, funding uncertainty, stakeholder churn. You’ll hold relationships through difficult periods and keep Accurx front of mind even when it’s not their immediate priority.

You should apply if...

  • You own relationships, not just accounts. You’ve worked in customer success, account management, or a relationship-heavy role and you know the difference between being a yes-person and being a trusted advisor. Accurx has no commission plan — success here is measured by trust, retention, and real outcomes.

  • You push back constructively. You don’t jump when a customer says jump. You ask why — more than once — and you find a better solution. You’re empathetic but not a pushover.

  • You’re comfortable building from scratch. Processes aren’t fully defined here. You’d rather create structure than wait for someone else to do it, and you’re okay if the first version isn’t perfect.

  • You’re curious about the NHS. Whether you’ve worked in or around it or you’re coming in fresh — you’re genuinely interested in how it works and patient enough to navigate its complexity.

  • You’re AI-native. You use AI tools to work smarter — automating the routine so you can spend more time on the things that actually need you.

  • You’re a natural connector. You’re as comfortable in a room with a clinical lead as you are with a Trust’s Head of Digital Transformation or a commercial director. You adapt your style and bring people with you.

SugarAI ships AI-powered selling and sales intelligence products in a market that moves faster every day. This is not a role for someone who favors traditional software development, or is curious about AI-assisted development and plans to explore it. It's a role for someone who already works this way who writes clear, machine-readable specifications that feed the agentic development system, uses agentic development tools as standard equipment, and applies genuine critical judgment to what these tools produce before it ships. You'll build systems and features that power real customer outcomes in a B2B SaaS platform at scale, and you'll do it inside a delivery model where human judgment is the differentiating input, not the bottleneck. 

If you want to work on meaningful software with teammates who hold the bar high on both speed and craft, this role is for you.

This role operates on a hybrid model, with a mix of remote work and in-office collaboration at our Solihull location, specifically, working in-office a minimum of 2 days per week.

Impact You Will Make in the Role (Key Responsibilities): 

Agentic Development Systems 

  • Work from executable specifications — write clear SDD/BDD specs and acceptance criteria as the primary input for AI-assisted code generation, and keep them current as implementation evolves 

  • Use agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or equivalents) as standard equipment across the full SDLC, from spec to implementation to test generation to code review

Feature Delivery 

  • Design, implement, and ship features and components that are reliable, maintainable, and built to perform in high volume, high-availability SaaS environments 

  • Ensure agentic code is clean, well tested, and follows the standards that make it easy to understand and extend by both agentic systems and your teammates 

  • Own your feature areas end-to-end, from understanding the requirement to production delivery, including identifying and resolving defects before they reach customers 

Code Quality & Review 

  • Review outputs, including AI-generated code and agentic attestations, with the care and rigor the team depends on; catch what automation misses 

  • Orchestrate unit and integration test development that verifies real behaviour, not just execution paths; apply the same critical eye to test quality as to production code 

  • Contribute to the team's technical standards and raise the bar on engineering operations excellence across all facets of our AI SDLC 

Collaboration & Systems Thinking 

  • Work closely with product managers, designers, and QA engineers to understand requirements and build the right thing, not just the specified thing 

  • Think beyond your immediate feature: understand the systems your code interacts with, the data it produces, and the downstream effects of your design decisions 

  • Communicate clearly in writing in specs, in code reviews, in async updatesto keep cross-functional and globally distributed teams aligned 

  • Participate in agile and team ceremonies, including Sprint Review, Program Reviews, and other technical presentations 


What You Will Bring (Qualifications/Experience): 

  • 2–5 years of experience developing enterprise or SaaS software in production environments 

  • Personal fluency with agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or equivalents) you use these in your daily work and real delivery scenarios, not as an experiment 

  • Hands-on experience with BDD/SDD frameworks and working from executable specifications as the primary input to development, this is how we work, not a practice you're learning on the job 

  • Proficiency in at least one object-oriented or modern SaaS language; comfort picking up new languages and frameworks as the work demands 

  • Experience with RESTful API design and consumption 

  • Working knowledge of SQL and NoSQL data stores 

  • Experience producing and maintaining automated test suites (unit, integration, or end-to-end) 

  • Experience working in Agile delivery environments with CI/CD pipelines 

  • Strong written communication skills; able to write clear specs, meaningful code review feedback, and async updates for a global team 


Preferred Qualifications/Experience: 

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS or equivalent) and microservices architectures 

  • Familiarity with containerization, infrastructure-as-code, or observability tooling 

  • Experience developing or integrating with AI/ML features in a production SaaS product 

  • Background in B2B SaaS, CRM, or revenue technology

We have a long list of candidate opportunities than we can fund, spanning payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance. We have a working hypothesis about which of these pays back first, and we'll share it — but part of the job in your first quarter is to pressure-test it, size the alternatives yourself, and tell us where to start.

This is a founding role, and for the first few quarters it is a building role more than a managing one. You'll be the only person in the function: doing the analysis, engineering the features, training and evaluating the models or agents, taking the first system live with our engineering teams — and then operating it, answerable for its uptime, its drift and its numbers. Once the first use cases are proving out, you'll hire and lead a hub-and-spoke team of data scientists and machine learning engineers embedded across our highest-value business areas. You'll report into the VP of Data and work in close partnership with Product, Payments, Engineering, Risk and Finance.

What you'll do: 

  • Prioritise which opportunities have the biggest impact.. Build a value-based use-case backlog across payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance; size the leading candidates properly; and make the call on sequencing with the relevant Product, Risk, RevOps and Finance stakeholders. This gets refreshed quarterly.

  • Personally deliver the first system end to end: the analysis and back-test, the features, the model, policy or agent, the deployment, and the shadow and A/B tests that prove it works. Not a spec handed to someone else to build.

  • Operate what you deploy. Own monitoring, retraining, drift response, incident handling and rollback for live decisioning, alongside the engineering teams whose services call it — and set the expectation that the function runs its systems rather than shipping them.

  • Work across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and be honest about which a problem actually needs: a propensity or uplift model, a policy of rules, or an agent with tools, evals against golden answer sets and trace-level observability. Several of our strongest candidate use cases point each way.

  • Build and lead the team — hire senior data scientists embedded in value areas and machine learning engineers in the hub, and set the professional standards, shared methods and reusable components the function runs on.

  • Establish the production stack alongside Data Platform and Engineering: reproducible training data, code and artefacts; a model registry; inference services with real latency, availability and rollback requirements; historically accurate features where decisions need backdated reconstruction; eval harnesses and trace observability for agentic workflows; and monitoring for data quality, drift, model performance and economic outcomes. Start ad hoc where that's sufficient and platformise once the first use cases have shown what's actually needed.

  • Own value capture end to end. Shadow-test and A/B test every deployment against the incumbent strategy, translate metric movement into a financial number on a methodology co-signed by Finance, and publish a quarterly report on realised value.

  • Set the governance model for automated decisioning — proportionate risk assessment, clear ownership, latency and availability requirements, human escalation and rollback — working with Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Risk on GDPR, EU AI Act and payments obligations, and producing the evidence early enough to shape the design.

  • Define the boundaries and the working relationship with Product Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Platform and AI Enablement, so accountability for decision support versus automated decisioning stays unambiguous.

  • Deliver cross-functionally: embed in delivery groups with product owners, domain experts and platform engineers rather than handing models over the wall.

We'd love to hear from you if you:

  • Experienced leading data science or ML teams that own systems in production, with deployments that moved a commercial metric and kept running afterwards. Proofs of concept and dashboards are not what we're hiring for.

  • Hands-on now, not formerly. Your first quarters are spent writing SQL and Python, engineering features, evaluating models and agents, and doing the work that gets a system live — not reviewing someone else's.

  • Experienced across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and clear about how they differ in practice: propensity and uplift models, feature pipelines and drift on one side; tool and context design, prompt and retrieval iteration, evals against golden answer sets and trace observability on the other.

  • Practised at running live systems rather than just launching them — monitoring, retraining, incident response, rollback, and the on-call reality of a decision the business depends on.

  • Pragmatic about method: happy to argue for rules or heuristics where they capture most of the value, and to reserve models and agents for where they genuinely earn their keep.

  • Comfortable with an undefined starting point. There's a long list of candidate use cases and a strong internal hypothesis, but no fixed roadmap — you'll be expected to form your own view, back it with numbers, and defend it to an executive audience.

  • Strong on measurement — experimentation, uplift modelling, back-testing — and willing to hold your own work to a financial number that Finance will scrutinise.

  • Fluent in the engineering side of production ML and agents (training pipelines, model registries, inference services, feature stores, drift detection, trace observability) and able to hold your own with senior engineers on latency, availability, observability and rollback.

  • Able to hire, level and develop senior data scientists and ML engineers, and to set standards for a function that doesn't exist yet.

  • Credible with executives and commercial stakeholders: you can take a use case from business problem to value estimate to prioritisation decision, and say no to low-value work.

  • Experienced in payments, fintech, subscriptions, high-volume commercial operations or another regulated transactional domain — enough to get to a credible value estimate in a new area quickly.

  • Comfortable treating regulated ML as a design constraint rather than paperwork — model risk assessment, DPIAs, auditability, traceability of model and policy versions to production decision logic.

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.


Our Values

  • Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”

  • Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple”

  • Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs”

Why you’ll love working at Paddle

We are a diverse, growing group of Paddlers across the globe who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We are a ‘digital-first’ company, which means you can work remotely, from one of our stylish hubs, or even a bit of both! We offer all team members unlimited holidays and 4 months paid family leave regardless of gender. We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

title: Channel Account Manager
description:
This is a field position. 

About the Position

The Channel Account Manager (CAM) responsibilities include working within the sales team to promote and sell network security products within a geographic territory. The CAM is responsible for supporting assigned WatchGuard partners in the assigned territory and will be responsible for active channel partners. The CAM will be responsible for quoting, training, lead generation and follow-up, event support, and the forecasting and tracking for their assigned partners. The CAM will report to the Country Manager, working closely to assure territory quota attainment, in addition to joining with the sales and field marketing teams in the territory. Success in this position will be measured by meeting successful transaction, growth, and retention goals with the assigned partners. The CAM will keep up-to-date knowledge of the industry and the competitive posture of the company, as well as prepare activity and forecast reports as requested.


Position Responsibilities

· Strive towards the territory quota attainment, retention, and growth/development of active partners

· Maintain regular contact with partners to ensure satisfaction and continued success

· Partner with Territory Channel Account Manager to generate new business and develop current customers through the partner network

· Support partners on standard methodologies and use of WatchGuard, including training, event support, and lead generation

· Create and perform sales presentations to match WatchGuard with audience needs

· Provide ongoing relationship management and training for partners

· Net growth for WatchGuard One Certifications in the territory

· Be knowledgeable of all WatchGuard products, services, and internal sales tools

· Other duties and projects assigned


Skills and Qualifications

· Experience with two-tier/channel sales ecosystem required

· Experience in network/cyber security space preferred

· History of sales experience with partner accounts

· History of consistent plan development and quota achievement

· Strong presentation and written skills

· Ability to self-manage and work remotely

· Familiarity with Salesforce or similar CRM


Experience

· 2+ years’ experience in direct and indirect sales in related industry

· Bachelor’s degree or equivalent training in business, sales, or marketing.


Why Work for WatchGuard?

WatchGuard is a global leader in network security and intelligence, advanced endpoint protection, multi-factor authentication, and secure Wi-Fi. Our award-winning products and services are trusted worldwide by more than 18,000 security resellers and service providers to protect more than 250,000 customers. Our technology keeps our customers ahead of increasingly sophisticated hackers and has fueled record revenues at WatchGuard.

WatchGuard is headquartered in Seattle, Washington, with team members working remotely and in offices worldwide.

Our company culture places an intense focus on our customers and employees. From the newest employee to our CEO, you'll find that each person at WatchGuard embodies our Core Values:

Accountability, Community, Belonging, Action, Innovation, and Customer-Centric. Learn more about our company culture at www.watchguard.com/wgrd-careers.

WatchGuard provides equal employment opportunities for all qualified employees, regardless of their race, color, national origin, religion, ancestry, creed, pregnancy, age, sex, sexual orientation (including gender expression or identity), marital status, mental or physical disability, honorably discharged veteran or military status or any other category protected by federal, state or local laws. Our equal employment opportunity (or EEO) policy focuses solely on the talent, hard work, contributions, and actual results achieved by each WatchGuard employee and on the potential of employment candidates to make such contributions. We consider focusing on an employee's protected characteristics rather than on talent, hard work, and actual work results to violate our EEO policy. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we are committed to a diverse workforce. WatchGuard participates in E-verify.

WatchGuard is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. Please let us know if you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability.

description:

Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team—from Finance to HR—to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.
 
Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally. Industry leaders like Unilever, Snowflake, Siemens, and DPD use Pigment daily to make more informed decisions and confidently navigate any scenario.

As a Solution Innovation Analyst, you will be the operational backbone of the Solution Innovation Center. You will support Account Executives and the wider GTM organisation with the day-to-day mechanics of getting RFPs, security reviews, and questionnaires completed accurately and on time, and help keep our Consensus demo automation platform and video content pipeline running smoothly. You will work cross-functionally on a regular basis, partnering with teams such as Legal and Security to get responses reviewed and signed off.       • Question Routing – Triage incoming Infosec questions, handling standard items directly from the answer library and routing anything technical to the Technical SC team.

        • Demo Automation Platform Administration (Consensus)

        • User Administration – Manage user access and permissions within Consensus, Pigment's demo automation platform.

        • Content Administration – Organise, tag, and maintain content within Consensus so that demo videos and Interactive Product Tours stay current and easy for the field to find.

          • Content Creation & Video Editing (Descript)

          • Content Support – Support the creation of demo videos and other digital content, using Descript to edit and produce assets for the Video demo library.

            • Cross-Functional Coordination

            • GTM Partnership – Act as a responsive point of contact for AEs on RFP status, timelines, and next steps.

            • Legal & Security Coordination – Work cross-functionally with teams such as Legal and Security to route questions, gather input, and get RFP and Infosec responses reviewed and signed off.

            • CSM Coordination – Support Post-Sales teams with the administrative steps of security and infosec review requests, routing them to the right owner.


    Who You Are:

    • Experience: Entry level or early career (1-3 years).  Some experience in the software industry or operational experience in an industry setting would be an advantage. No prior presales experience required.

    • Location & Language: Based in our Paris office, with fluency in English required.

    • Organised & Detail-Oriented: Comfortable managing multiple requests at once, with a strong eye for accuracy and consistency in written material.  You must be able to work under pressure and manage tight deadlines.

    • Process-Minded: Enjoys bringing structure and reliability to operational workflows, and takes ownership of the tasks in front of them.

    • Proactive Communicator: Openly communicates status, roadblocks, and concerns with the SIC team and stakeholders across GTM.

    • Coachable: Takes ownership of individual learning, asks questions, and seeks support on assigned tasks as they ramp.

    • AI-Proficient: Comfortable using AI tools to automate process workflows and improve day-to-day efficiency, and keen to keep exploring new ways AI can streamline operational work.

    • Collaborative: Works well within the SIC team and with outside teams (AEs, Post-Sales, Legal, Security, Product) when called upon.

  • Proven experience with Financial Consolidation (FC) tools, such as Oracle HFM, Oracle FCCS, SAP Financial Consolidation (fka Cartesis) / Group Reporting/ BPC, OneStream, Fluence, or Tagetik.
  • Experience with other EPM solutions, Close Management Solutions, and/or Disclosure Management solutions is a plus.
  • Background in pre-sales (Solution Consulting) at a SaaS/software company or finance transformation, with a strong record of engaging finance teams in adopting consolidation solutions.
  • Strong understanding of legal and management consolidation, intercompany eliminations, IFRS/local GAAP compliance, cash flow reporting, and audit requirements.
  • Understanding of non financial reporting requirements (CSRD, Pilar 2 tax reporting, etc…)
  • BA/BS in Finance, Accounting, or a related field; DSCG or DEC (or UK equivalents) preferred.

title: Optimisation AI Scientist
description:
Join Pigment: Transforming Business Planning and Performance with AI  
 
Founded in 2019, Pigment stands out as one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally, redefining business planning and performance with our AI-powered platform. We empower organizations across diverse industries, including Consumer Packaged Goods, Retail, and Technology, to seamlessly integrate data, people, and processes, enabling them to plan and adapt rapidly.  
 
With a vibrant team of over 500 professionals across North America and Europe, and offices in Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, Pigment has successfully secured nearly $400 million in funding from leading global venture capitalists. Our recognition as a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software underscores our commitment to excellence, as we proudly partner with industry leaders like Unilever, Vinci, Kayak, Siemens, and Coca-Cola.  
 
At Pigment, we champion smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo—all as a united team. Every team member has the opportunity to make a significant impact and tackle ambitious challenges. Together, we pursue excellence with a collaborative spirit, continuously raising the bar to ensure strong performance and a proactive approach while fostering an environment of humility.  
 
If you are passionate about innovation and wish to collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry, we would love to hear from you!

We are hiring an Optimisation AI Scientist to own the technical delivery of Pigment's solver pilot programme and build the foundations of a production-grade optimisation capability - moving customers from descriptive planning to prescriptive, solver-driven decision-making.

This role is partially customer-facing: leading and shaping the formulation of each client's optimisation problem, directly involved in implementations.

What you will do:

  • Formulate supply chain optimisation problems as rigorous mathematical models - objective functions, costs, penalties, and constraints

  • Configure and run optimisation models for customer pilots and implementation, and support Solutions Architects in delivering results and debriefs

  • Build and run Python models against third-party solvers across multiple dataset scales, and benchmark results across use cases

  • Work with Engineering and Data Science leads to define the path to production-grade solver integration and customer specific implementations within Pigment's architecture

  • Engage technically with solver vendor teams during partnership evaluation

Who you are and what you can do:

  • Demonstrable experience formulating and solving optimisation problems for real-world operational use cases

  • Proficiency in Python with hands-on experience in a major solver library (Gurobi, OR-Tools, CPLEX, HiGHS, or equivalent)

  • Experience with supply chain/operations data — SKUs, BOMs, capacity constraints, service levels, lead times, inventory targets etc.

  • Understanding of core OR techniques: branch-and-bound, LP relaxation, constraint programming, sensitivity analysis

  • Degree in Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Industrial Engineering, CS, or related field (MS/PhD advantageous)

Role Overview

We’re building category-defining AI products for Finance, Planning and Operations professionals and the market is moving fast. Pigment is looking for a Head of Brand Marketing to serve as a key architect of our brand’s long-term evolution.

We're hiring a Head of Brand Marketing to own how Pigment shows up in the world: visually, verbally, culturally, and emotionally. You'll be the senior leader most responsible for what Pigment feels like in a keynote, on a billboard, in a product launch film, on a t-shirt at a conference. The goal isn't brand-as-decoration. It's a compounding advantage: the reason a great engineer or sales leader joins us over a competitor, the reason a CFO remembers our name in a procurement meeting, the reason a journalist picks up our story.


What you'll do:
  • You work closely with the CMO and senior leadership on the brand's long-term evolution. 
  • Bring the brand to life in a way that is clear, compelling, and deeply customer-centered, championing bold ideas and high standards, translating strategy into stories and experiences
  • You’ll build a brand with a real point of view. Not one that hedges toward consensus.
  • You’ll own Pigment's visual and creative identity. That means making calls on direction and driving consistency in execution across every customer touchpoint.
  • Own the development and governance of naming and nomenclature across products and experiences, ensuring a clear, consistent, connected brand system
  • Lead the creation of compelling brand stories, campaigns, and narratives that emotionally connect users with Pigments purpose.
  • You lead the in-house creative team: You are responsible for their development, their creative output, and the culture of the team. You set the quality bar and you hold it.
  • You also personally build. Depending on the week, that means designing a campaign asset, writing a brand narrative section, or art-directing a shoot.
  • Use AI as an operating principle to drive efficiencies and scale but not at the expense of producing lower quality outputs.
  • You drive the operating model for how creative work gets reviewed, who provides input at which stage, and where final approval sits. 
  • You own Agency and freelance relationships at strategy and execution level, managing iterative design development across multi-stakeholder projects and synthesizing internal feedback and direction
  • You define how we track brand health: distinctiveness, awareness, branded search trends, and influence.

    • Who You Are:

    You have defined and led a brand at a B2B company, ideally SaaS.  Your portfolio includes work you personally made, not only work you directed.

    You have run agency relationships, not just managed them. You know the difference between directing an agency and supervising one. 

    You are a credible partner to senior leadership. You can present brand rationale at board level, take input from the CEO

    You are AI-fluent in practice. You use AI tools in your creative workflow: for prototyping, for expanding what you can produce, for speed. You have formed clear opinions about when they add value and when they don't.

  • 10 years of experience in brand strategy (in-house or agency) with at least 3 years owning brand direction at a company with a defined visual identity
  • Experience within a high-growth B2B or SaaS environment and a portfolio of B2B or enterprise brand work, including work you personally made
  • Comfortable diving into market data and research reports but possess the brand gut to know which insights actually matter
  • Can distill complex products and market dynamics into a clear, compelling narrative that inspires designers, writers, and executives alike
  • Know how to influence without authority and build strong partnerships with creative leads to drive the best possible work
  • Direct experience leading and developing in-house designers

At Pigment, we are rewriting the rules of business planning. To build the future of our own product, our internal Finance team must operate like a high-performing engineering squad. We don't just execute tasks; we architect systems.
 
As a Finance Engineer, you will sit at the crossroads of Accounting logic, Systems Architecture, and Generative AI. Reporting directly to the Head of FinOps, your mission is to treat the entire Finance stack as a machine: designing automated data pipelines, building production-ready apps via Pigment's Modeller Agents, and ensuring our financial infrastructure scales seamlessly as we grow. The position is Hybrid, meaning 3x per week from the office, no remote possibilities.

What Will You Do:

1. Systems Architecture & Modeling (50%)

  • Architect the Machine: Design, build, and optimize multidimensional models and process within Pigment for internal Accounting (P2P, QTC,R2R,..), Cash Management, and RevOps use cases.
  • Bridge the Gap: Translate complex accounting policies, billing structures, and revenue recognition rules into clean, scalable, logic-based data flows.
  • Tool-Agnostic Infrastructure: Ensure seamless data mapping between upstream systems (Zip, Navan, Salesforce) and our ERP ecosystem (Netsuite), maintaining a bulletproof "single source of truth."

    • 2. AI Engineering & Process Automation (30%)

  • Prompt Engineering & Agents: Leverage LLMs and Pigment’s native AI capabilities to build automated reporting agents.
  • Smart Automation: Deploy workflows (via Workflow automation tool : N8N or APIs,…) to automate month-end closing tasks, anomaly detection, and real-time cash forecasting.
  • Continuous Close: Actively scout and test next-generation Fintech tools to move the Finance department toward a fully automated, real-time audit-ready state.

    • 3. Governance, Support & Evolution (20%)

  • Code Mentality: Maintain clear technical documentation, schemas, and playbooks for our finance stack—treating financial logic with the same rigor as product code.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with the existing FP&A Modeler/Architect to maintain a unified data dictionary across the entire company.
  • Long-term Roadmap: Support the team's evolution as we prepare to fully internalize and optimize our ERP (NetSuite) architecture in early 2027.

    • Who You Are:
  • Experience: 3 to 6 years of experience in FinOps, RevOps, or as a Finance Business Analyst / Analytics Engineer within a fast-growing tech/SaaS company.
  • The "Builder" Mindset: High skills in multidimensional modeling (Pigment, PowerBi,…) or a strong background in data manipulation (Advanced SQL, Python, or expert-level logic).
    AI-Curious: You understand how to prompt LLMs, use APIs, and are excited about deploying AI agents to replace repetitive human processes.
  • Financial Fluency: You understand Accounting principles, P&L mechanics, and Cash flows. You can hold a deep conversation with our Finance team and translate their requirements into system logic.
  • Education: Degree in Engineering, Data Science, MIAGE, or Business School with a heavy focus on Business Intelligence / Information Systems.

Deliver: You make a difference every day in the engineering team(s) you are working with, as you enhance clarity, direction, scope, and keep all the parts together with other roles (such as Product Managers). title: Technical Project Manager - Engineering Delivery
description:
Diabolocom is looking for a Technical Project Manager to coordinate engineering delivery across our organization and work closely with the Head of Software Engineering on roadmap execution.

You will work across Engineering, Product, Infrastructure and Project teams to keep delivery on track, manage dependencies, identify risks early, and help turn delivery challenges into clear actions and decisions.

We are looking for someone with a software engineering background who has moved into technical leadership and genuinely enjoys the operational side of engineering.

The role

Our engineering organization includes around 90 engineers across 12 teams, working on a complex global product and multiple parallel initiatives.

This role combines ownership of our engineering delivery processes with hands-on execution. You will be responsible not only for running these processes, but also for continuously improving how we plan, coordinate and track delivery across the organization.

Process ownership

You will own and continuously improve:

  • engineering delivery planning processes
  • delivery tracking and reporting
  • cross-team coordination and dependency management.

You will build on our existing practices and ClickUp workflows, identifying what can work better and evolving the processes as the organization and product develop.

Delivery execution

Day to day, you will:

  • track delivery across teams and releases
  • coordinate dependencies and clarify ownership across teams
  • identify risks, blockers and delivery gaps early
  • challenge unclear timelines, priorities and commitments
  • coordinate next steps when delivery is at risk
  • provide clear visibility on delivery status and progress.

You will work closely with Engineering, Product, Infrastructure and Project teams to facilitate alignment.

The objective is simple: make software delivery predictable, transparent and effective.

What success looks like

First few weeks: You start taking ownership of delivery operations and become effective in coordinating ongoing delivery.

Within ~6-8 weeks: You understand the roadmap, teams, dependencies and delivery processes well enough to manage them confidently and start identifying opportunities for improvement.

Within 3 months: You operate autonomously across day-to-day engineering delivery coordination, bringing in the Head of Software Engineering when decisions or trade-offs require escalation.

Your work will directly influence our delivery efficiency and predictability: how much we can take on and how reliably we deliver what we commit to.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for someone who started in software engineering and moved into technical leadership, for example, an Engineering Manager, Technical Lead, senior Team Lead, or Technical Program Manager.

Titles matter less than scope. You need enough technical depth to understand architecture and dependencies, ask the right questions, and navigate complex delivery problems across teams.

We expect

  • around 10 years of experience in software engineering environments
  • at least 3 years in engineering or technical leadership
  • previous hands-on experience as a software engineer
  • experience leading or coordinating multiple engineering teams
  • a track record of delivering complex software initiatives and improving execution
  • strong understanding of the software development lifecycle, distributed systems and cross-team dependencies
  • understanding of Product Management fundamentals
  • experience with Agile and structured project management frameworks such as PMBOK or similar
  • strong prioritization, decision-making and communication skills
  • professional fluency in English.

French and Russian are nice to have.

This role will suit you if…

You still enjoy technical complexity, but what really motivates you is making execution work.

You like finding out why something is stuck and fixing it.

You genuinely enjoy the operational side of engineering: creating structure, improving processes, coordinating teams and making sure things get delivered.

You don’t just want to follow an established process. You naturally look for ways to make it work better.

You are comfortable working across multiple teams, asking difficult questions when needed, and bringing structure to situations where priorities, dependencies or timelines are not immediately clear.

Why Diabolocom

Diabolocom is building one of Europe’s most advanced AI-native CCaaS platforms, powering business-critical customer interactions for 400+ enterprise and mid-market customers across 60+ countries.

We combine a mature global CCaaS platform with a rapidly growing AI Product Suite, backed by our internal AI Research Lab and proprietary AI innovation.

Our ambition goes beyond adding AI features to an existing product. We are building toward a platform capable of orchestrating AI agents, human agents, business workflows and communication channels, with CCaaS as the execution layer.

For Engineering, this means working on the technical and operational challenges of an established enterprise product, from real-time communications and distributed systems to complex integrations, while contributing to its next generation.

With teams across Europe, the US, Brazil and the UAE, and an engineering organization of around 90 people, this role offers the opportunity to work on engineering delivery behind a global product used for critical customer operations.

Why this role

This is a hands-on role combining delivery execution with process ownership.

You will work with the Head of Software Engineering, Team Leads, Product, Infrastructure and Project teams, with a broad view of engineering delivery across the organization.

You will inherit established delivery practices, own them, and continuously improve how we plan, coordinate and track execution.

title: Head of Infrastructure
description:
Build the infrastructure behind the next generation of AI-powered customer communications

Diabolocom is building an AI-first communication platform where AI agents, human agents, business workflows and communication channels work together seamlessly.

As we enter our next phase of growth, we are looking for a Head of Infrastructure to own and scale the infrastructure foundation behind this platform.

This is a unique opportunity to lead an infrastructure organization combining carrier-grade voice systems, on-premise data centers, distributed systems and AI workloads, while building the operational maturity required to support 2x growth.

You will report directly to Sergei, our CTO, and lead the infrastructure organization — owning operational excellence, team development and execution of infrastructure initiatives, while actively contributing to technical strategy and architecture decisions.

Why this role is different

Most infrastructure leadership roles today focus on managing cloud platforms and abstracted services. Here, you will own the foundations of a real-time, AI-first communication platform — from hardware and networks to telecom systems, distributed services, and operational processes.

Our philosophy is simple: we build and operate our infrastructure ourselves. 100% of our production infrastructure is managed by our teams, giving us full technical ownership, deep system knowledge, and the ability to solve complex challenges without relying on external vendors. This allows us to move faster, make better architectural decisions, and build systems tailored to our needs.

You will work across:

  • Telecom infrastructure — we are a global voice carrier powering real-time communications across multiple markets. We manage carrier relationships, routing decisions, and voice traffic flows end-to-end, with the expertise and tooling built internally.
  • On-premise infrastructure — around 95% of our production infrastructure runs on our own hardware across several data centers around the Paris and Frankfurt areas, with servers, networking, and connectivity fully managed by our teams.
  • Cloud infrastructure — while the majority of our production runs on-premise, we strategically leverage cloud services for remote locations and specific workloads where they provide faster deployment and operational efficiency, particularly for smaller-scale deployments.
  • Stateful systems — PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis, and others powering high-volume workloads.
  • Distributed systems — the platform is deployed in a fully redundant way across multiple data centers, with the ability to sustain the loss of a data center without impacting workloads.
  • AI infrastructure — GPU workloads and compute infrastructure supporting our AI capabilities.
  • Storage system — Ceph provides our main object and volume storage layer, supporting all other services across the infrastructure.

This is infrastructure engineering where reliability, latency, scalability, and operational excellence directly impact the product.

You will not simply maintain existing systems. You will help shape the architecture, processes, and team structure required for the next stage of our growth — taking ownership of critical infrastructure decisions from the ground up.

Your mission

Your goal is to make infrastructure ready for the next stage of scaling up by building a strong operational foundation across all the infrastructure domains.

You will:

  • Own infrastructure reliability and operations across the whole stack: incident management, monitoring, alerting, post-mortems and prevention of recurring failures.
  • Improve operational visibility across infrastructure teams: identify bottlenecks, improve processes and drive continuous improvements.
  • Improve capacity planning processes, connecting business growth and infrastructure needs.
  • Lead the evolution of our network and telecom infrastructure: topology, connectivity, carrier relationships, routing, redundancy and voice platform performance and reliability.
  • Own our on-premise infrastructure operations: data centers, hardware, storage, connectivity and deployment practices.
  • Drive scalability and reliability of our stateful infrastructure: PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis and other critical systems.
  • Support the evolution of our AI infrastructure, including GPU workloads and compute clusters.
  • Drive infrastructure improvements with automation, observability and tooling.
  • Partner with engineering teams to ensure applications run reliably on our platforms.
  • Lead and grow the Infrastructure team across Networking, SRE, Stateful Systems, Voice, and Data Center squads.

Who we are looking for

We are not looking for someone who has mastered every infrastructure domain.

We are looking for a strong infrastructure engineer and leader who has built complex systems, understands operational excellence and wants broader ownership.

You might be:

  • a Head of Infrastructure looking for a more hands-on technical challenge;
  • an Infrastructure Manager who still enjoys engineering;
  • a Staff/Principal SRE who has been leading infrastructure beyond their formal title;
  • a network or systems engineer who grew into technical leadership.

Must Have

  • Deep expertise in at least 2–3 infrastructure domains, such as:
    • networking;
    • SRE/reliability;
    • database administration;
    • telecom/voice infrastructure;
    • hardware/on-premise infrastructure.
  • Proven experience building and improving infrastructure operations: establishing processes, improving reliability practices, driving incident management and creating effective ways of working across multiple infrastructure domains.
  • Experience leading technical teams where different groups own different areas of infrastructure (for example networking, SRE, databases, systems or platform engineering).
  • Strong hands-on mindset: you stay close to technology, understand technical details and lead through context and expertise.
  • Self-taught, hands-on background — you have grown technically by solving complex problems beyond your formal role.
  • Fluent English, both written and spoken. French or other languages are a plus.
  • Ability to work onsite in Paris.

Nice to Have

Experience with:

  • Telecom or carrier infrastructure.
  • Voice platforms or real-time communication systems.
  • PostgreSQL, Kafka, RabbitMQ or Redis operational experience at scale.
  • Dark fiber, peering and advanced networking.
  • Kubernetes in production.
  • GPU infrastructure.
  • Incident command and post-mortem culture.

About You

You are motivated by complexity and ownership, not titles.

You solve problems before being asked.

You are comfortable with ambiguity — infrastructure is complex, and you know how to make pragmatic technical trade-offs.

You enjoy building teams and scaling impact through people, not only systems.

You stay curious about networking, hardware trends, observability and modern infrastructure practices.

Why join us

Own infrastructure decisions with real business impact.

Your work will directly influence reliability, customer experience and engineering velocity.

Work on infrastructure that cannot simply be outsourced.

From telecom networks and hardware to distributed systems and AI workloads, you will solve problems where architecture and engineering decisions matter.

Build something from an early stage of maturity.

You will help establish the operational discipline, processes and team structure needed for the next phase of growth.

Work directly with technical leadership.

You will report directly to Sergey, our CTO, who is deeply involved in infrastructure and technical decisions while giving infrastructure leaders the ownership to drive changes.

title: Maintenance Technician
description:
Société
Le Groupe IRCA est l’un des principaux fournisseurs internationaux d’ingrédients semi-finis pour les marchés de la boulangerie, de la pâtisserie et de la glace, s’adressant aussi bien aux producteurs indépendants qu’aux grands industriels de l’agroalimentaire (CPG). Ses produits incluent notamment le chocolat, les décorations en chocolat, les crèmes, les mixes pour la boulangerie, les ingrédients pour la glace et d’autres ingrédients de pâtisserie.
En 2023, l’entreprise – dont le siège est en Italie – a acquis RAVIFRUIT, une marque premium de purées de fruits située à Anneyron, en France.
RAVIFRUIT est une marque mondiale qui produit des purées et préparations de fruits de haute qualité pour les circuits Gourmet et PME, distribuant dans plus de 65 pays.

Objectif du poste

description:

vivenu s’engage auprès de ses partenaires pour assurer un support d’excellence et pour répondre de façon simple à leurs enjeux en créant des expériences exceptionnelles.
 
Rejoignez-nous et participez à la transformation des métiers de la billetterie et du marketing.

  •  Interface produit / ingénierie : assurer l’interface entre vos clients et les équipes produit et techniques. Traduire les retours clients en spécifications techniques détaillées pour influencer directement la feuille de route logicielle de vivenu.

  • Gestion de portefeuille et priorisation : expérience dans la gestion d'un portefeuille de clients, avec la capacité de gérer efficacement le temps et les ressources en fonction des besoins, des objectifs et des indicateurs de performance de vos clients.
